questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to study in the United States to understand more about their culture and how their college is structured.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was the best 5 months of my life. So many new friends and fun memories.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was not that hard to find the information, but there just was a lot of practical things that had to be done. Like reading a lot of document, answering a lot of questions about the stay and meeting at the embassy to get my VISA.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a welcome meeting for all international students at the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It wasn't too bad. However most only offer 12 months leases which is too long for someone studying abroad. My advise would simply just be to reach out to as many landlords as possible and try and get in contact with them (CONTACT THEM EVEN THOUGH THEY SAY THEY ONLY DO 12 MONTHS LEASES). And start early!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's way cheaper than living on campus and you get better rooms. Also the university had a bunch of busses that you could track only and use to get to campus. And the busses are free for students!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It can be pretty hard to find something for only 4-6 months.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It's an online platform that you can acces from the university app. Be aware you can only registrer in designated time periods. But you can start looking at classes before that. As an international student I had some problems with prerequisites in the portal, but just email your academic advisor and they can fix it so you can actually sign up for the classes you want.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could contact your academic advisor.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware you can only registrer in designated time periods. But you can start looking at classes before that. As an international student I had some problems with prerequisites in the portal, but just email your academic advisor and they can fix it so you can actually sign up for the classes you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was bachelor classes. I took one math, one chemistry and one physics

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I prefer the UCPH method a lot more. At my host institution it was mainly lecture and then maybe a weekly 45 minute discussion session. So there were no classes where you could sit with a TA and just do problems. Instead it was heavily focused on homework assignments which should be done in your own time. This means you have a lot of free time and not a lot of classes. Think I maybe had like 12 hours a week in total. Which is nice but also means you have to spend more time doing your homework assignments. 
Also in some classes attendance counts towards your grade. And they have more tests since they also have midterms.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Quantum Chemistry 
Galactic Structure and Interstellar Medium 
Applied Statistics and Machine Learning

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Applied Statistics and Machine Learning. Amazing class. Learned so much and it is taught really well. It is not the most easy class, but it is very rewarding and interesting.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There's A LOT of clubs. Almost one for any interest. The sports were mainly on campus so not that much to choose between.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There's were so many clubs. Both cultural, religious and scientific. Also there's an office of student involvement that regularly had events. There's also sororities and fraternities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Maybe one of the sports clubs or any club that interests them. Also the sororities/fraternities were fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to Yosemite!!! Do hikes around El Capitan, Half Dome and go see Tunnel View. Also Sequoia National Park is a must - go see the world biggest trees. Both in Yosemite and Sequoia the stargazing is amazing. 
Visit San Fransisco, Los Angelas and San Diego.
Do a roadtrip down highway 1. 
Go to Vegas. 
And many more. So many cool things to do.  
Go to hawaii when your semester ends. You are "so close" to Hawaii compared to normally and it is soooo nice there.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy. Not a big culture chok

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are more talkative than in Denmark so just initiate conversations and be open to new experiences.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
It can be a little difficult not to have a car. Since their cities from an infrastructural point of view are designed for cars it can be a little difficult to get around. 
Solution: Take Lyft, Uber or get your friends to take you!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed the diversity. It is way more diverse than I am used to in Denmark which I really like. It is fun to experience so many different cultures at once and also seeing them interact with each other.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't be shy! Chat up everyone and make new connections. They love to show you around and take you out to try new "local" experiences. Also engage in clubs or similar activities to get additional friends apart from those in your classes. 
Take advantage of the delivery culture. You can get anything delivered to you door which is soooo convenient (don't be lazy though).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask the locals where they buy their stuff (groceries etc.). I went to Food4less a lot since it was cheaper than many other options. But just ask your friends what they do.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the new friends I made and the memories I made with them. Have so many fun and unforgettable memories with these people and can't wait for them to come visit me in Denmark and for me to come back and visit them.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sometimes balancing the social with the school. I like to do well in the school and at the same time there was always so many social things happening. But as long as you make a schedule and manage your time well it should be good.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy! It is the best/the most fun time of your life.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
